conditions: architecture documents validate against referenced schemas
limitations: CALM pattern semantics must be mapped to AIW without replacing AIW canonical IDs
objects.statement: CALM represents architecture patterns as reusable machine-readable constraints that can be validated against concrete architectures.

conditions: personal data is stored in event payloads
limitations: The exact regulatory solution depends on jurisdiction and legal interpretation
objects.statement: Immutable event stores can conflict with data-erasure obligations, so sensitive personal data should be separated or protected with a deliberate deletion strategy.

conditions: catalog data is aggregated from multiple systems
limitations: Some organizations may designate the catalog as authoritative for selected ownership metadata
objects.statement: A developer portal catalog should be treated as a synchronized discovery and caching layer rather than the ultimate architecture source of truth.

conditions: implementation is available as Java bytecode
limitations: It does not validate runtime topology or business rationale
objects.statement: ArchUnit can turn approved Java architecture dependency and layering decisions into executable unit-test rules.

limitations: Language and framework coverage depends on available plugins
objects.statement: jQAssistant can scan software artifacts into a graph and evaluate architecture constraints, making it useful for intended-versus-implemented architecture comparison.

limitations: OAM is deployment-oriented and does not replace domain/application architecture modelling
objects.statement: OAM separates application workload components from operational traits, policies and workflows, supporting clearer responsibility boundaries.

conditions: domain experts and technical participants collaborate
limitations: Outputs require facilitation and are hypotheses until validated against delivery/runtime evidence
objects.statement: The DDD starter modelling process combines several collaborative techniques to validate domain boundaries and message flows iteratively.

conditions: used as a reference fixture, not a universal blueprint
limitations: The demo intentionally contains teaching scenarios and optional failure modes

provenance.heading: Welcome to the OpenTelemetry Astronomy Shop Demo

objects.statement: The OpenTelemetry demo provides a useful test corpus for observability topology, telemetry dependencies and failure-simulation scenarios.

conditions: pattern schema and target mesh capabilities are compatible
limitations: Configuration validity is not proof that a mesh is needed
objects.statement: Service-mesh configurations can be captured as reusable declarative patterns and imported as topology plus policy metadata.

conditions: Java or Kotlin codebase adopts the supported abstractions or annotations
limitations: Annotations and interfaces express intent but do not prove that domain boundaries are correct
objects.statement: jMolecules can express DDD building blocks, events and architectural styles in code and connect those declarations to ArchUnit or jQAssistant verification.

conditions: application uses Spring Boot and a compatible module-detection strategy
limitations: Tool-detected modules do not replace domain modelling or architecture review
objects.statement: Spring Modulith can discover and verify application modules, test them independently, observe module interactions and generate documentation from the implemented module arrangement.

conditions: CML constructs are mapped to stable AIW semantic identities
limitations: Context maps cover strategic domain boundaries and do not replace application, technology or deployment views
objects.statement: Context Mapper DSL provides a machine-readable representation of strategic DDD context maps and service-decomposition models that can be imported into and exported from AIW.

conditions: schema versions and component identifiers are mapped explicitly
limitations: Meshery topology validity does not establish application-architecture suitability

provenance.heading: Visually and collaboratively manage your infrastructure

objects.statement: Meshery models and design templates can provide component, relationship and topology metadata for an AIW deployment-view adapter.

conditions: metadata is kept distinct from suitability evidence
limitations: The landscape is a discovery taxonomy, not a pattern or best-practice authority
objects.statement: The CNCF Landscape Graph can enrich AIW technology discovery and taxonomy metadata, but landscape inclusion must not be interpreted as architectural endorsement.

componentKit.name: Microservices Application Boundary
componentKit.responsibility: Own business responsibility and dependency direction

componentKit.name: Microservices Application Core
componentKit.responsibility: Implement use cases without infrastructure coupling

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Microservices intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Microservices

exclusions: Avoid when one small team owns the whole product and coordinated releases are acceptable.
Avoid when domain boundaries are uncertain; begin with a modular monolith and extract only after evidence.
Do not use microservices merely to separate technical layers or to imitate a reference architecture.
mitigations: Use domain boundaries and dependency direction tests to prevent technical-layer services.
Prefer asynchronous integration for non-immediate workflows and define explicit consistency semantics.
Adopt a paved platform path, service ownership catalogue and service-level objectives before scaling the service count.
objects.name: Microservices

obligations.description: Assign accountable ownership, measurable acceptance criteria and review cadence for Microservices.
obligations.title: Own Microservices lifecycle
obligations.verificationHint: The architecture decision links an owner, quality scenario and review date.

obligations.description: Define telemetry, failure handling and fitness functions that prove the intended Microservices properties.
obligations.title: Validate Microservices in operation
obligations.verificationHint: Automated tests and runtime evidence are attached to the architecture decision.

prerequisites: Bounded contexts or capability ownership are documented.
API and event contract governance is available.
Central identity, secrets, observability and deployment automation are production-ready.
risks: Chatty synchronous dependencies can create a distributed monolith with worse reliability than the original system.
Duplicated data and eventual consistency can surprise business users and reconciliation processes.
Service proliferation increases platform, security, observability and on-call burden.
objects.summary: An independently deployable service architecture that aligns service boundaries to business capabilities and accepts distributed-systems complexity in exchange for team autonomy, selective scaling and fault isolation.

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Saga Boundary intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Saga Boundary

exclusions: Avoid for operations that require immediate atomic consistency across all participants.
Do not model irreversible financial settlement as a simple technical rollback.
Avoid choreography when participants cannot understand the full process or event ownership.
mitigations: Prefer orchestration when process visibility and controlled sequencing are critical.
Model compensations as new auditable business actions, not hidden rollbacks.
Provide operations with stuck-saga queues, replay controls and manual resolution runbooks.
objects.name: Saga Boundary

obligations.description: Assign accountable ownership, measurable acceptance criteria and review cadence for Saga Boundary.
obligations.title: Own Saga Boundary lifecycle
obligations.verificationHint: The architecture decision links an owner, quality scenario and review date.

obligations.description: Define telemetry, failure handling and fitness functions that prove the intended Saga Boundary properties.
obligations.title: Validate Saga Boundary in operation
obligations.verificationHint: Automated tests and runtime evidence are attached to the architecture decision.

prerequisites: A canonical process state model and correlation ID are defined.
Timeouts, retries, compensation and manual resolution paths are documented.
Audit evidence records each state transition and actor.
risks: Compensation may not restore the original business state after external side effects.
Choreographed sagas can become difficult to understand and change safely.
Retries and timeouts can trigger duplicate actions without strict idempotency.
objects.summary: Coordinates a long-running business transaction across autonomous services as a sequence of local transactions with explicit compensating actions and observable business state.

componentKit.name: Transactional Outbox Integration Edge
componentKit.responsibility: Mediate protocol, policy and flow control

componentKit.name: Transactional Outbox Message or API Contract
Transactional Outbox Failure Channel
componentKit.responsibility: Capture retry, dead-letter and recovery behaviour

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Transactional Outbox intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Transactional Outbox

exclusions: Do not use as a substitute for consumer idempotency or message schema governance.
Avoid when the source store cannot atomically persist the business record and outbox entry.
Do not claim exactly-once end-to-end delivery; publication and consumption remain at-least-once in most implementations.
mitigations: Alert on oldest unpublished row, relay failure rate and backlog size.
Use immutable event IDs, monotonic aggregate versions and idempotent consumers.
Define retention and replay procedures that preserve audit and privacy obligations.
objects.name: Transactional Outbox

obligations.description: Own relay availability, backlog age, retries, poison records, retention and replay procedures.
obligations.title: Operate and monitor the outbox relay
obligations.verificationHint: Alert on oldest unpublished record and prove replay from a controlled checkpoint.

obligations.description: Every emitted message carries a stable event identifier and consumers suppress duplicate effects.
obligations.title: Enforce downstream idempotency
obligations.verificationHint: Run duplicate-delivery tests and verify one business effect per event identifier.

prerequisites: A stable event identifier and idempotency key strategy are defined.
Outbox retention, retry, poison-message and replay procedures are owned.
Event schemas and compatibility policy are governed.
risks: Relay lag can delay downstream visibility and hide growing operational debt.
Poor partitioning or ordering keys can publish related events out of business order.
Deleting outbox rows too early can make recovery or audit impossible.
objects.summary: Atomically records a domain change and an outbound message in the same local transaction, then publishes the message asynchronously so database state and integration events cannot diverge through a dual-write failure.

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted CQRS intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for CQRS

exclusions: Avoid for ordinary CRUD systems where one model meets performance and maintainability needs.
Do not introduce separate stores before projection ownership and rebuild procedures exist.
Do not assume CQRS requires event sourcing; they are independent choices.
mitigations: Expose projection freshness and define business-specific staleness budgets.
Keep command and query separation limited to justified boundaries.
Version projection logic and test full rebuilds using production-scale data.
objects.name: CQRS

obligations.description: Assign accountable ownership, measurable acceptance criteria and review cadence for CQRS.
obligations.title: Own CQRS lifecycle
obligations.verificationHint: The architecture decision links an owner, quality scenario and review date.

obligations.description: Define telemetry, failure handling and fitness functions that prove the intended CQRS properties.
obligations.title: Validate CQRS in operation
obligations.verificationHint: Automated tests and runtime evidence are attached to the architecture decision.

prerequisites: Command validation, idempotency and authorization are defined.
Projection rebuild, versioning and reconciliation procedures are tested.
User experience explains stale or pending read states where relevant.
risks: Projection lag can cause users or downstream systems to act on stale state.
Duplicated schemas and handlers increase maintenance and testing effort.
Rebuilds can overload the source or take too long after schema changes.
objects.summary: Separates command and query models when write invariants and read workloads require materially different models, scaling or optimization paths.

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Event Sourcing intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Event Sourcing

exclusions: Avoid when current-state CRUD fully satisfies audit and reporting needs.
Do not store raw sensitive data in immutable events without an approved erasure or crypto-shredding strategy.
Do not use event sourcing solely to obtain an integration event stream.
mitigations: Keep external effects outside replayable projection handlers.
Use event versioning, upcasters and contract tests before publication.
Tokenize or segregate sensitive data and maintain an approved erasure strategy.
objects.name: Event Sourcing

obligations.description: Assign accountable ownership, measurable acceptance criteria and review cadence for Event Sourcing.
obligations.title: Own Event Sourcing lifecycle
obligations.verificationHint: The architecture decision links an owner, quality scenario and review date.

obligations.description: Define telemetry, failure handling and fitness functions that prove the intended Event Sourcing properties.
obligations.title: Validate Event Sourcing in operation
obligations.verificationHint: Automated tests and runtime evidence are attached to the architecture decision.

prerequisites: Event schema compatibility, upcasting and ownership policies are defined.
Snapshot and projection rebuild procedures are tested at expected data volume.
Privacy, retention and legal-hold requirements are mapped to event payload design.
risks: Event schema mistakes persist for the lifetime of the stream and complicate replay.
Replaying old events can repeat external side effects if boundaries are not strict.
Immutable personal data can conflict with erasure obligations.
objects.summary: Stores domain state as an ordered sequence of immutable events and derives current views by replay, providing temporal audit and alternative projections at the cost of event lifecycle complexity.

componentKit.name: Circuit Breaker Resilience Policy
componentKit.responsibility: Apply timeout, retry, isolation or shedding

componentKit.name: Circuit Breaker Reliability Telemetry
componentKit.responsibility: Expose saturation, errors and recovery evidence

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Circuit Breaker intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Circuit Breaker

exclusions: Do not use without timeouts; a circuit breaker cannot interrupt an indefinitely blocked call.
Do not wrap local in-process calls where ordinary exception handling is sufficient.
Avoid using fallback data when stale or incomplete results could create financial or safety harm.
mitigations: Tune from measured latency and error distributions rather than fixed folklore values.
Use jittered half-open probes and expose breaker state in dashboards and alerts.
Make degraded responses explicit and traceable to the affected dependency.
objects.name: Circuit Breaker

obligations.description: Timeout, failure threshold, open duration and half-open probes are derived from measured dependency behavior.
obligations.title: Calibrate breaker thresholds from dependency SLOs
obligations.verificationHint: Load and failure tests demonstrate bounded resource use and controlled recovery.

obligations.description: Operations can see state transitions, rejected calls, fallback use and affected business capabilities.
obligations.title: Expose breaker state and degraded behavior
obligations.verificationHint: Dashboards and alerts identify open circuits and fallback rates per dependency.

prerequisites: Dependency SLOs, timeout budgets and failure thresholds are defined.
Metrics expose open/half-open state, rejection rate and downstream health.
Retry policies use jitter and are coordinated with the breaker.
risks: Poor thresholds can oscillate between open and closed states or reject healthy traffic.
A fallback can conceal prolonged dependency failure and create silent data quality issues.
Independent breakers across many instances can synchronize recovery probes.
objects.summary: Stops repeated calls to a failing or slow dependency after a threshold, fails fast during an open interval and probes controlled recovery to limit cascading failure.

componentKit.name: Retry with Backoff Resilience Policy
componentKit.responsibility: Apply timeout, retry, isolation or shedding

componentKit.name: Retry with Backoff Reliability Telemetry
componentKit.responsibility: Expose saturation, errors and recovery evidence

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Retry with Backoff intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Retry with Backoff

exclusions: Never retry non-idempotent operations without a stable idempotency key.
Do not retry validation, authorization or permanent business failures.
Do not layer independent retries at multiple tiers without a shared end-to-end budget.
mitigations: Use exponential backoff with full jitter and a shared retry budget.
Track retry amplification and stop when the error is permanent or the circuit is open.
Prefer asynchronous redelivery for long recovery windows.
objects.name: Retry with Backoff

obligations.description: Assign accountable ownership, measurable acceptance criteria and review cadence for Retry with Backoff.
obligations.title: Own Retry with Backoff lifecycle
obligations.verificationHint: The architecture decision links an owner, quality scenario and review date.

obligations.description: Define telemetry, failure handling and fitness functions that prove the intended Retry with Backoff properties.
obligations.title: Validate Retry with Backoff in operation
obligations.verificationHint: Automated tests and runtime evidence are attached to the architecture decision.

prerequisites: Timeouts are shorter than retry and request budgets.
Circuit breaker and load-shedding behavior are coordinated.
Duplicate suppression or idempotency is tested.
risks: Nested retries can create exponential traffic multiplication.
Long retry windows can hold scarce resources and violate user latency targets.
Retrying during overload can prevent the dependency from recovering.
objects.summary: Retries transient failures after increasing, jittered delays within a bounded attempt and time budget so recovery does not amplify load on an unhealthy dependency.

conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Bulkhead

exclusions: Do not create arbitrary partitions that share the same hidden downstream bottleneck.

Do not use bulkheads as a substitute for capacity planning or dependency SLOs.
mitigations: Validate end-to-end failure domains, including downstream pools and quotas.
Base limits on measured demand and adjust using saturation and rejection metrics.
Combine with load shedding and clear priority policies.

obligations.verificationHint: The architecture decision links an owner, quality scenario and review date.

obligations.description: Define telemetry, failure handling and fitness functions that prove the intended Bulkhead properties.
obligations.title: Validate Bulkhead in operation
obligations.verificationHint: Automated tests and runtime evidence are attached to the architecture decision.

prerequisites: Workload classes, priorities and capacity assumptions are documented.
Load tests verify isolation and graceful rejection.
Operational procedures allow safe tuning without restart where possible.
risks: Over-partitioning can waste capacity and reduce total throughput.
Incorrect limits can starve a critical workload or hide a capacity shortage.
Partitions may not isolate failures if they converge on the same database or broker.
objects.summary: Partitions execution, connection or queue capacity so exhaustion in one workload, tenant or dependency cannot consume all resources needed by unrelated work.

componentKit.name: Zero Trust Protected Workload
componentKit.responsibility: Request access with workload or user identity

componentKit.name: Zero Trust Trust Service
componentKit.responsibility: Issue, validate or rotate trust material

conformanceRules.rationale: Preserve the accepted Zero Trust intent in implementation and deployment evidence.
conformanceRules.title: Conformance for Zero Trust

exclusions: Do not equate zero trust with a single product, VPN replacement or network micro-segmentation alone.
Avoid central policy dependencies without resilient local enforcement and safe failure modes.
Do not collect device or behavioral telemetry without privacy and retention controls.
mitigations: Use a common policy model, decision logs and automated tests for critical authorization paths.
Cache bounded policy decisions safely and design explicit fail-open/fail-closed behavior per risk.
Measure user and service impact and provide governed emergency access.
objects.name: Zero Trust

obligations.description: Authentication strength, least-privilege policy, credential lifetime and revocation are centrally governed and tested.
obligations.title: Govern policy and identity lifecycle
obligations.verificationHint: Policy tests cover critical allow, deny and break-glass paths.

obligations.description: Each protected operation has approved fail-open or fail-closed behavior and resilient policy enforcement.
obligations.title: Design policy-service failure behavior
obligations.verificationHint: Failure exercises verify the approved behavior without uncontrolled access.

prerequisites: Identity lifecycle, device posture and workload identity foundations are mature.
Policy-as-code, secrets management and certificate rotation are automated.
Break-glass access and policy outage behavior are approved and tested.
risks: Policy sprawl can create inconsistent access decisions and difficult incident diagnosis.
Identity or policy service failure can become a broad availability dependency.
Overly aggressive controls can impair frontline or low-connectivity operations.
objects.summary: Applies continuous identity, device, workload and context verification with least-privilege authorization at each protected interaction instead of trusting network location.
